p: The reader: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Nuʿaym al-Laythī al-Madanī, of Iṣfahānī origin, was born in Madinah around 70 AH and died there in 169 AH. He learned from more than seventy Successors, among them Abū Jaʿfar, and became the chief reciter of Madinah.
Qālūn: ʿĪsā ibn Mīnā ibn Wardān (120–220 AH), stepson of Nāfiʿ, who nicknamed him Qālūn (good) for his fine recitation. He succeeded Nāfiʿ as the leading reciter of Madinah.
Warsh: Abū Saʿīd ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Miṣrī (110–197 AH). He travelled to Madinah in 155 AH to read to Nāfiʿ, then returned to lead the reciters of Egypt.
The way followed: the Shāṭibiyyah, Imām al-Shāṭibī's poem on the seven readings; for Warsh this is the ṭarīq of al-Azraq. Comparisons are with Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim.
Beginning a sūrah: every reader recites the basmalah at the start of any sūrah except al-Tawbah.
Between two sūrahs, Qālūn: the basmalah only.
Between two sūrahs, Warsh: three ways: the basmalah; sakt, a short breathless pause; or waṣl, joining directly. Of the two ways without basmalah, sakt is preferred.

The four Zuhr sūrahs (al-Qiyāmah, al-Muṭaffifīn, al-Balad, al-Humazah): for Warsh, some scholars preferred sakt before them for one who otherwise joins, and the basmalah for one who otherwise makes sakt.
Al-Anfāl and al-Tawbah: no basmalah for anyone; the reciter stops, makes sakt, or joins.
Sūrat al-Fātiḥah: both read مَلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ without alif, where Ḥafṣ reads مَٰلِكِ, and neither counts the basmalah as one of its verses.
Before a sākin: like all readers, both give the mīm a ḍammah without lengthening, as in عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ (2:216).
Before a vowelled letter, Qālūn: two ways in waṣl: sukūn (preferred), or ṣilah, a ḍammah lengthened into a wāw of two ḥarakāt, as in رَزَقْنَٰهُمُۥ يُنفِقُونَ (2:3). Ḥafṣ always reads sukūn.
Before a vowelled letter, Warsh: sukūn, unless the letter is hamzat al-qaṭʿ.

Before hamzat al-qaṭʿ: Warsh must read ṣilah, lengthened six ḥarakāt as madd munfaṣil, as in وَمِنْهُمُۥٓ أُمِّيُّونَ (2:78). Qālūn keeps his two ways, his ṣilah taking his munfaṣil length, two or four.
In waqf: everyone stops on the mīm with sukūn.

General rule: as with Ḥafṣ, a hāʾ between two vowelled letters takes ṣilah of two ḥarakāt, as in رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ (87:15); before hamzat al-qaṭʿ it is lengthened as madd munfaṣil, as in مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا (92:11).

Words Qālūn reads short: a kasrah without ṣilah in يُؤَدِّهِ (3:75, twice), نُؤْتِهِ (3:145, twice; 42:20), نُوَلِّهِ and وَنُصْلِهِ (4:115), أَرْجِهِ (7:111; 26:36), وَيَتَّقِهِ (24:52) and فَأَلْقِهِ (27:28). Warsh reads them all with ṣilah, as in يُوَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيْكَ and أَرْجِهِۦ. Ḥafṣ has a sākin hāʾ in أَرْجِهْ and فَأَلْقِهْ, and alone reads وَيَتَّقْهِ with a sākin qāf.
يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا (20:75): Qālūn reads it short (preferred) or with ṣilah; Warsh with ṣilah.
يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ (39:7): Qālūn reads a ḍammah without ṣilah, as Ḥafṣ does.
Kasrah where Ḥafṣ has ḍammah: both read أَنسَىٰنِيهِ (18:63) and عَلَيْهِ ٱللَّهَ (48:10) with a kasrah on the hāʾ, so the lām of the Divine Name in the latter is thin.
فِيهِ مُهَانًا (25:69): both read it without ṣilah; Ḥafṣ lengthens it.
Madd muttaṣil: four ḥarakāt for Qālūn, six for Warsh, as in جَآءَ and سُوٓءٍ.
Madd munfaṣil: Qālūn reads two ḥarakāt (preferred) or four; Warsh six only, as in فِيٓ أُمِّهَا (28:59).

أَنَا before a hamzah: in waṣl Nāfiʿ pronounces its alif before a hamzah with fatḥah or ḍammah, as madd munfaṣil: أَنَآ أُحْيِۦ (2:258), وَأَنَآ أَوَّلُ (6:163). Before a hamzah with kasrah, as in أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ (26:115), Warsh drops the alif and Qālūn may keep or drop it. Before other letters it is dropped, as with Ḥafṣ.

Madd al-badal, Warsh: a madd letter after a hamzah, as in ءَامَنُوا, أُوتُوا, إِيمَانًا, is read with two, four or six ḥarakāt, in waṣl and waqf, even when the hamzah has been changed by naql, ibdāl or tashīl, as in ٱلَاخِرَةُ. This lengthening is particular to Warsh.

Exceptions to the badal: two ḥarakāt only in إِسْرَآءِيلَ; in the forms of يُوَاخِذُ; after a sound sākin in the same word, as in ٱلْقُرْءَانُ and مَسْـُٔولًا; when beginning verbs such as إِيتِ and أُوتُمِنَ; and in the alif that replaces tanwīn in waqf, as in دُعَآءً. عَادًا ٱلُّولَىٰ (53:50) and ءَآلَٰنَ (10:51, 91) have both ways, the three lengths or qaṣr alone.

Madd al-līn al-mahmūz, Warsh: a sākin wāw or yāʾ after a fatḥah and before a hamzah in the same word, as in شَيْءٍ, سَوْءَةَ, كَهَيْـَٔةِ, is read with four or six ḥarakāt in waṣl and waqf. With the hamzah in the next word there is only naql. Without a hamzah, līn is lengthened only in waqf, as for everyone.

Exceptions to the līn: no lengthening in مَوْئِلًا (18:58) and ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ (81:8). In سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا and its like, either the wāw is short with any of the three badal lengths, or wāw and badal are both four.

General rule, Qālūn: after the interrogative hamzah he reads the second hamzah, whatever its vowel, with tashīl (between a hamzah and the letter of its vowel) and inserts an alif between the two (idkhāl): ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ (2:6), أَءِذَا, أَءُنزِلَ (38:8). Ḥafṣ pronounces both fully.

General rule, Warsh: tashīl without idkhāl. If the second hamzah has a fatḥah he may also change it into an alif, six ḥarakāt before a sākin, as in ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ, and two before a vowelled letter, as in ءَأَلِدُ (11:72). In waqf on ءَأَنتَ or أَرَءَيْتَ only tashīl is read.
أَءُشْهِدُوا (43:19): Nāfiʿ reads two hamzahs, the second with ḍammah and tashīl, and a sākin shīn; Ḥafṣ reads أَشَهِدُوا. Qālūn has idkhāl or none; Warsh none.
ءَأَٰمَنتُمْ (7:123; 20:71; 26:49) and ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا (43:58): tashīl of the second hamzah only, with no idkhāl for Qālūn and no ibdāl for Warsh; Warsh has the three badal lengths after it.
أَئِمَّةً: tashīl of the second hamzah without idkhāl, for both.

Hamzat al-waṣl after the interrogative: in ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ (6:143, 144), ءَآللَّهُ (10:59; 27:59) and ءَآلْـَٰٔنَ (10:51, 91) all readers either change hamzat al-waṣl into an alif of six ḥarakāt (preferred) or read tashīl.

Repeated question (istifhām mukarrar): in the eleven passages like أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًا أَءِنَّا (13:5) Nāfiʿ reads a question first and a statement second, إِنَّا. In al-Naml (27:67) and al-ʿAnkabūt (29:28–29) he reverses this: إِذَا then أَئِنَّا, and إِنَّكُمْ then أَئِنَّكُمْ. Each transmitter applies his own rule to the question.
Scope: a hamzah ending one word meets a hamzah beginning the next, in waṣl; after a stop the second word begins with a full hamzah. Ḥafṣ pronounces both.
Different vowels, first with fatḥah: both read the second hamzah with tashīl: تَفِيٓءَ إِلَىٰ (49:9), جَآءَ أُمَّةً (23:44).

Different vowels, second with fatḥah: both change it into a wāw with fatḥah after ḍammah, ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ أَلَآ (2:13) read ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَآ, and a yāʾ with fatḥah after kasrah, ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةً (26:4) read ٱلسَّمَآءِ يَايَةً.
Different vowels, ḍammah then kasrah: both change the second into a wāw with kasrah (preferred) or read tashīl: يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ (2:142).

Same vowels, Qālūn: he alters the first hamzah. Two fatḥahs: he drops it, جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا (11:40) read جَا أَمْرُنَا, with two ḥarakāt (preferred) or four in the madd. Two kasrahs or ḍammahs: tashīl of the first, هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن (2:31), أَوْلِيَآءُ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ (46:32), with four ḥarakāt (preferred) or two in the madd before it.
بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا (12:53), Qālūn: besides tashīl, he may change the first hamzah into a wāw and merge the preceding wāw into it: بِٱلسُّوِّ إِلَّا.

Same vowels, Warsh: he alters the second hamzah, by tashīl or by changing it into a madd letter: six ḥarakāt before a sākin, as in جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا and هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن, two before a vowelled letter, as in جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ (6:61).

Warsh, special cases: if the following sākin takes an incidental vowel, both six and two are allowed, as in ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِنِ ٱتَّقَيْتُنَّ (33:32). جَآءَ ءَالَ (15:61; 54:41) has five ways: tashīl with the three badal lengths, and ibdāl with two or six. In هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن (2:31) and ٱلْبِغَآءِ إِنْ (24:33) a third way is a yāʾ with a light kasrah.

Sākin hamzah, Warsh: when it is the first root letter (fāʾ) of the word he changes it into a madd letter matching the preceding vowel: يُومِنُونَ, يَاكُلُ, يَامُرُ, فَاتُوا; also across words in waṣl, as in لِقَآءَنَا ٱيتِ (10:15). Qālūn keeps the hamzah, like Ḥafṣ.

Exceptions, Warsh: the hamzah stays in words derived from al-īwāʾ, such as ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ and تُـْٔوِيهِ, and when it is not the first root letter, as in شِئْتَ, except in بِيسَ, بِيرٍ (22:45) and ٱلذِّيبُ.
Hamzah with fatḥah after ḍammah, Warsh: as first root letter it becomes a wāw with fatḥah: يُوَاخِذُ, مُوَجَّلًا (3:145), مُوَذِّنٌ; otherwise it stays, as in فُؤَادَ.
Words without hamzah, Warsh: لِيَلَّا for لِئَلَّا, لِيَهَبَ (19:19) and ٱلنَّسِيُّ (9:37). Qālūn has both لِأَهَبَ and لِيَهَبَ.
Words without hamzah, Qālūn: وَرِيًّا (19:74), and لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنْ (33:50) and بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلَّا (33:53) with a doubled yāʾ in waṣl.
Hamzah added by Nāfiʿ: ٱلنَّبِيٓءُ, ٱلنَّبِيٓـِٔينَ, ٱلْأَنۢبِئَآءَ, ٱلنُّبُوٓءَةَ with madd muttaṣil; also ٱلْبَرِيٓـَٔةِ (98:6, 7), زَكَرِيَّآءَ, مِيكَآئِلَ (2:98), هُزُؤًا, كُفُؤًا.

هَٰٓأَنتُمْ (3:66, 119; 4:109; 47:38): Qālūn reads an alif of two or four ḥarakāt after the hāʾ, then a hamzah with tashīl. Warsh reads no alif: هَأَنتُمْ with tashīl, or the hamzah changed into an alif of six ḥarakāt.
أَرَءَيْتَ and its forms: Qālūn reads the second hamzah with tashīl; Warsh with tashīl or, in waṣl, as an alif of six ḥarakāt.
ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي (33:4; 58:2; 65:4), Warsh: no yāʾ; in waṣl a hamzah with tashīl after an alif of six or two ḥarakāt; in waqf a sākin yāʾ in place of the hamzah with six ḥarakāt, or tashīl with rawm.

Naql, Warsh: when a word ends in a sound sākin and the next begins with hamzat al-qaṭʿ, he moves the hamzah's vowel onto the sākin and drops the hamzah: قَدَ افْلَحَ (23:1), مَنَ امَنَ, قُلُ اوحِيَ (72:1). The sākin may be tanwīn, كُفُؤًا اَحَدٌ (112:4); a līn letter, خَلَوِا اِلَىٰ (2:14); or the lām of the article, ٱلَارْضِ, ٱلِانسَٰنُ.
Where there is no naql: into mīm al-jamʿ, into a madd letter, or inside one word, as in ٱلْقُرْءَانُ.

Beginning after naql to the article: Warsh begins with hamzat al-waṣl, اَلَرْضِ, or with the lām, لَرْضِ. A badal in the word, as in ٱلَاخِرَةِ, takes its three lengths with hamzat al-waṣl and qaṣr only with the lām.
كِتَٰبِيَهْ إِنِّي (69:19–20), Warsh: the sounder way is no naql, with sakt in مَالِيَهْ هَلَكَ (69:28–29); the other is naql here and idghām there.
Naql, Qālūn: none, except in the three words that follow.
رِدًا (28:34): both read it so, where Ḥafṣ reads رِدْءًا; it is the only naql inside a word.

ءَآلْـَٰٔنَ (10:51, 91): both move the last hamzah's fatḥah to the lām: ءَآلَٰنَ. Hamzat al-waṣl is then an alif of six ḥarakāt, an alif of two (the lām now being vowelled), or read with tashīl. With the badal lengths Warsh has seven ways in waṣl and nine in waqf.

عَادًا ٱلْأُولَىٰ (53:50): Nāfiʿ merges the tanwīn into the lām, which takes the hamzah's ḍammah. Warsh reads عَادًا ٱلُّولَىٰ; Qālūn adds a sākin hamzah, عَادًا ٱلُّؤْلَىٰ. Beginning the second word, Qālūn reads ٱلْأُولَىٰ like Ḥafṣ (preferred), ٱلُؤْلَىٰ or لُؤْلَىٰ; Warsh ٱلُولَىٰ or لُولَىٰ.
Dhāl of إِذْ, lām of هَلْ and بَلْ: Nāfiʿ reads iẓhār before all their letters, as Ḥafṣ does.
Dāl of قَدْ: Warsh merges it into ḍād and ẓāʾ: فَقَد ضَّلَّ, فَقَد ظَّلَمَ (2:231). Qālūn reads iẓhār, like Ḥafṣ.
Tāʾ al-taʾnīth: Warsh merges it into ẓāʾ: كَانَت ظَّالِمَةً (21:11), حُرِّمَت ظُّهُورُهَا (6:138). Qālūn reads iẓhār.
Dhāl before tāʾ: both merge it in ٱتَّخَذتُّمْ, أَخَذتُّمْ and their like; Ḥafṣ reads iẓhār.
وَيُعَذِّبْ مَن يَشَآءُ (2:284): Nāfiʿ reads فَيَغْفِرْ and وَيُعَذِّبْ with sukūn. Qālūn merges the bāʾ into the mīm; Warsh reads iẓhār.
ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا (11:42) and يَلْهَث ذَّٰلِكَ (7:176): Qālūn has idghām (preferred) and iẓhār; Warsh iẓhār.
يسٓ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ and نٓ وَٱلْقَلَمِ: Warsh merges the nūn into the wāw in the first and has both ways in the second; Qālūn reads iẓhār in both.
The sakt of Ḥafṣ: neither makes it. They join عِوَجًا قَيِّمًا (18:1–2) and مَرْقَدِنَا هَٰذَا (36:52), and merge in مَن رَّاقٍ (75:27) and بَل رَّانَ (83:14).
Qālūn: fatḥ everywhere, including مُجْرَىٰهَا (11:41), which Ḥafṣ reads with imālah. Exceptions: ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ, read with fatḥ (preferred) or taqlīl, and هَارٍ (9:109), read with imālah.

Warsh, dhawāt al-rāʾ: taqlīl (a slight inclination of the alif towards yāʾ) only, in waṣl and waqf, in a final alif written as yāʾ after a rāʾ, as in تَرَىٰ, بُشْرَىٰ, ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ, and in an alif before a final rāʾ with kasrah, as in ٱلنَّارِ, ٱلْأَبْرَارِ, أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ; also in كَٰفِرِينَ and ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ.

Dhawāt al-rāʾ read otherwise: fatḥ in ٱلْجَوَارِ, بِضَآرِّهِمْ, مُضَآرٍّ, أَنصَارِيٓ, and where the rāʾ is not final, as in نَمَارِقُ and فَلَا تُمَارِ. Both fatḥ and taqlīl in أَرَىٰكَهُمْ (8:43), جَبَّارِينَ (5:22; 26:130) and وَٱلْجَارِ (4:36).
Warsh, dhawāt al-yāʾ: both fatḥ and taqlīl in a final alif that goes back to yāʾ or is written as yāʾ: ٱلْهُدَىٰ, مُوسَىٰ, أَتَىٰ, ٱلدُّنْيَا, بَلَىٰ, مَتَىٰ, عَسَىٰ, أَنَّىٰ.
No taqlīl: لَدَى, عَلَىٰ, إِلَىٰ, حَتَّىٰ, مَا زَكَىٰ (24:21); three-letter words whose alif goes back to wāw, as دَعَا and ٱلصَّفَا; and مَرْضَاتِ, كِلَاهُمَا, ٱلرِّبَوٰا, كَمِشْكَوٰةٍ.

Verse endings: in Ṭā Hā, al-Najm, al-Maʿārij, al-Qiyāmah, al-Nāziʿāt, ʿAbasa, al-Aʿlā, al-Shams, al-Layl, al-Ḍuḥā and al-ʿAlaq Warsh reads verse-final dhawāt al-yāʾ with taqlīl only, except the endings in هَا.
Opening letters: Warsh reads taqlīl in the rāʾ of الٓر and الٓمٓر, the hāʾ and yāʾ of كٓهيعٓصٓ and the ḥāʾ of حمٓ, and full imālah in the hāʾ of طه.
رَءَا: before a vowelled letter Warsh reads taqlīl in the rāʾ and the hamzah, as in رَءَا كَوْكَبًا (6:76); before a sākin, as in رَءَا ٱلْقَمَرَ (6:77), fatḥ in waṣl and taqlīl only in waqf.
Alif dropped in waṣl: where tanwīn or a following sākin removes the alif, as in هُدًى and مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ, taqlīl is possible only in waqf.

Link with the badal, Warsh: in one passage, qaṣr of the badal goes with fatḥ of dhawāt al-yāʾ, tawassuṭ with taqlīl, and ṭūl with both, as in فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ (2:37). Dhawāt al-rāʾ are not tied to the badal.

Warsh's rule: he alone reads a rāʾ with fatḥah or ḍammah thin (tarqīq), in waṣl and waqf, after a sākin yāʾ or a permanent kasrah in the same word: خَيْرًا, قَدِيرٌ, يُبْصِرُونَ, ٱلَاخِرَةُ. Other readers read these thick.
A sākin between kasrah and rāʾ: tarqīq remains, as in ٱلسِّحْرَ and إِخْرَاجًا, unless the sākin is ṣād, ṭāʾ or qāf: مِصْرَ, قِطْرًا, وِقْرًا.

Thick despite the kasrah: non-Arabic names, إِبْرَٰهِيمَ, إِسْرَآءِيلَ, عِمْرَٰنَ, and إِرَمَ (89:7); a letter of istiʿlāʾ after the rāʾ, even beyond an alif: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ, إِعْرَاضًا, ٱلْفِرَاقُ; a repeated rāʾ: فِرَارًا, ضِرَارًا, مِدْرَارًا, إِسْرَارًا; a kasrah or yāʾ in another word or prefix, or an incidental kasrah: بِرَسُولٍ, فِي رَيْبٍ, إِنِ ٱرْتَبْتُمْ; and a vowelled yāʾ before it: ٱلْخِيَرَةُ.
بِشَرَرٍ (77:32): Warsh reads the first rāʾ thin, following the second.
Two ways: حَيْرَانَ (6:71), and the six words ذِكْرًا, سِتْرًا, وِزْرًا, إِمْرًا, حِجْرًا, صِهْرًا; in the six, only tafkhīm is read with tawassuṭ of the badal.
With taqlīl: the rāʾ of dhawāt al-rāʾ is thin.

Warsh's rule: he thickens (taghlīẓ) a lām with fatḥah, single or doubled, after ṣād, ṭāʾ or ẓāʾ carrying fatḥah or sukūn: ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ, ظَلَمُوا, ٱلطَّلَٰقُ, مَطْلَعِ, أَظْلَمَ, إِصْلَٰحًا. If a condition is missing the lām is thin, as in ظُلِمَ and ضَلَّ.
Two ways, taghlīẓ preferred: when an alif separates the two letters, أَفَطَالَ (20:86), فِصَالًا (2:233), يَصَّٰلَحَا (4:128); and in waqf on a final lām, as in ظَلَّ, فَصَلَ, يُوصَلَ.

Lām before an alif of taqlīl: in يَصْلَىٰ, سَيَصْلَىٰ, يَصْلَىٰهَا, and مُصَلًّى (2:125) in waqf, taghlīẓ goes with fatḥ and tarqīq with taqlīl. In the taqlīl-only verse endings وَلَا صَلَّىٰ (75:31), فَصَلَّىٰ (87:15), إِذَا صَلَّىٰ (96:10) the lām is thin.

Lengths: all readers allow two, four or six ḥarakāt in madd ʿāriḍ lil-sukūn and in līn; in līn mahmūz Warsh keeps to four or six. When a badal becomes ʿāriḍ, as in مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ, Warsh stops with no less than the badal length he is reading.
Dropped in waqf: the ṣilah of mīm al-jamʿ and the yāʾāt al-zawāʾid.
Beginning: after a stop the second of two meeting hamzahs is begun in full; verbs like ٱئْتِ and ٱؤْتُمِنَ are begun by everyone as إِيتِ and أُوتُمِنَ.

Definition: the first-person yāʾ attached to a word and written in the muṣḥaf; the readers differ over 212 of them, between fatḥah and sukūn. A sākin yāʾ before hamzat al-qaṭʿ is lengthened as madd munfaṣil.

Before a hamzah with fatḥah (99): Nāfiʿ reads fatḥah, as in إِنِّيَ أَعْلَمُ (2:30), where Ḥafṣ has sukūn. Sākin for all: أَرِنِيٓ أَنظُرْ (7:143), تَفْتِنِّيٓ أَلَا (9:49), فَٱتَّبِعْنِيٓ أَهْدِكَ (19:43), وَتَرْحَمْنِيٓ أَكُن (11:47). Sākin for Nāfiʿ too: ذَرُونِيٓ أَقْتُلْ (40:26), ٱدْعُونِيٓ أَسْتَجِبْ (40:60), فَٱذْكُرُونِيٓ أَذْكُرْكُمْ (2:152). In أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ (27:19; 46:15) Qālūn reads sukūn, Warsh fatḥah.

Before a hamzah with kasrah (52): Nāfiʿ reads fatḥah, as in مِنِّيَ إِلَّا (2:249). Both read sukūn in أَنظِرْنِيٓ (7:14), فَأَنظِرْنِيٓ (15:36; 38:79), يُصَدِّقْنِيٓ (28:34), أَخَّرْتَنِيٓ (63:10), يَدْعُونَنِيٓ (12:33), تَدْعُونَنِيٓ (40:41, 43) and ذُرِّيَّتِيٓ (46:15). In إِخْوَتِي إِنَّ (12:100) Qālūn reads sukūn, Warsh fatḥah. In رَبِّي إِنَّ لِي (41:50) Qālūn has fatḥah (preferred) and sukūn.
Before a hamzah with ḍammah (10): fatḥah, as in إِنِّيَ أُعِيذُهَا (3:36), except بِعَهْدِيٓ أُوفِ (2:40) and ءَاتُونِيٓ أُفْرِغْ (18:96), sākin for all.
Before the definite article (14): fatḥah in all, as in عَهْدِيَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ (2:124), where Ḥafṣ has sukūn.

Before hamzat al-waṣl alone (7): sukūn in إِنِّي ٱصْطَفَيْتُكَ (7:144), أَخِي ٱشْدُدْ (20:30–31), يَٰلَيْتَنِي ٱتَّخَذتُّ (25:27); fatḥah in لِنَفْسِيَ ٱذْهَبْ (20:41–42), ذِكْرِيَ ٱذْهَبَا (20:42–43), قَوْمِيَ ٱتَّخَذُوا (25:30), بَعْدِيَ ٱسْمُهُۥ (61:6).

Before other letters (30): sukūn, except that both read fatḥah in وَجْهِيَ (3:20; 6:79), بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ (2:125; 22:26), وَمَمَاتِيَ (6:162), وَمَا لِيَ (36:22) and وَلِيَ دِينِ (109:6), and Warsh also in وَلْيُومِنُوا بِيَ (2:186), وَلِيَ فِيهَا (20:18), مَّعِيَ (26:118) and تُومِنُوا لِيَ (44:21). Nāfiʿ reads بَيْتِي مُؤْمِنًا (71:28) with sukūn.
وَمَحْيَايْ (6:162): Qālūn reads a sākin yāʾ after an alif of six ḥarakāt. Warsh reads that or a yāʾ with fatḥah, with fatḥ or taqlīl of the alif.

Definition: final yāʾs that some readers pronounce although the muṣḥaf does not write them; the Shāṭibiyyah counts 62. Nāfiʿ pronounces those he keeps in waṣl and drops them in waqf. Such a yāʾ is lengthened as madd munfaṣil before hamzat al-qaṭʿ and falls away before a sākin.
Kept by Qālūn only: إِن تَرَنِۦ (18:39) and ٱتَّبِعُونِۦٓ أَهْدِكُمْ (40:38).
ٱلتَّلَاقِ (40:15), ٱلتَّنَادِ (40:32), ٱلدَّاعِ and دَعَانِ (2:186), Qālūn: two ways in waṣl, dropping the yāʾ (preferred) or keeping it.
ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ (27:36): both read a yāʾ with fatḥah in waṣl. In waqf Warsh drops it; Qālūn drops it or keeps it sākin.
يَٰعِبَادِي لَا خَوْفٌ (43:68): both read a sākin yāʾ in waṣl and waqf.

First of two sākins: when a final sākin meets a verb beginning with hamzat al-waṣl whose third letter has a permanent ḍammah, Nāfiʿ gives that sākin a ḍammah where Ḥafṣ gives a kasrah: قُلُ ٱدْعُوا ٱللَّهَ أَوُ ٱدْعُوا (17:110), وَقَالَتُ ٱخْرُجْ (12:31), وَلَقَدُ ٱسْتُهْزِئَ (6:10), and the tanwīn in مَحْظُورًا ٱنظُرْ (17:20–21).
Ishmām: both read سِيٓءَ (11:77) and سِيٓـَٔتْ (67:27) with a kasrah on the sīn that begins with a touch of ḍammah, without any wāw.

Sukūn where Ḥafṣ has ḍammah: both read خُطْوَٰتِ with a sākin ṭāʾ; أُكْلَهَا, ٱلْأُكْلِ and أُكْلٍ with a sākin kāf; and وَٱلْأُذْنَ بِٱلْأُذْنِ (5:45), أُذْنٌ (9:61) and أُذْنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ (69:12) with a sākin dhāl.
يَحْسِبُ: both read the present tense of this verb with a kasrah on the sīn, as in يَحْسِبُهُمُ; Ḥafṣ reads a fatḥah.
وَهْوَ and وَهْيَ, Qālūn: he reads the hāʾ of هُوَ and هِيَ sākin after wāw, fāʾ or lām, as in وَهْوَ, فَهْوَ, لَهْوَ, وَهْيَ, and in ثُمَّ هْوَ (28:61).

Ikhtilās, Qālūn: he shortens the kasrah of the ʿayn in نِعِمَّا (2:271; 4:58), and the fatḥah of the ʿayn, hāʾ and khāʾ in لَا تَعَدُّوا (4:154), يَهَدِّي (10:35) and يَخَصِّمُونَ (36:49), to about two-thirds of a vowel; he may also read these letters sākin. Warsh reads a full fatḥah in the last three. Ḥafṣ reads لَا تَعْدُوا, يَهِدِّي, يَخِصِّمُونَ.

Other words: Nāfiʿ reads نِسْيًا (19:23), تَسَّٰقَطْ (19:25), مُخْلِصًا (19:51), جُثِيًّا, عُتِيًّا and صُلِيًّا (19:8, 68–72), فَيَسْحَتَكُم (20:61), تَلَقَّفْ (20:69), قُل رَّبِّي يَعْلَمُ (21:4) and قُل رَّبِّ ٱحْكُم (21:112); also يَٰبُنَيِّ, تَذَّكَّرُونَ and يُحْزِنكَ.
